title: Opposition (basic: T1-2 depth only)

D0.outcome: Describes the opposition: the two kings face each other on a file or rank with one square between them, and the side that does not have to move holds the opposition.

D1.outcome: In a king-and-pawn ending, when told to find the winning (or drawing) move, finds the move that takes (or keeps) the opposition.

D2.outcome: In a king-and-pawn ending with no hint, decides whether the side with the pawn wins or only draws, and finds the only move that keeps the win or the draw.

D3.outcome: Names two situations the basic rule does not cover (a pawn still on its starting rank, a rook pawn) and checks such positions with the tablebase lab instead of trusting the rule.

misconceptions: The opposition means moving next to the enemy king (kings can never touch).
Having the opposition means it is your move; it is the side NOT to move that has it.
The opposition always decides a king-and-pawn ending.
conditions: The side that does not have to move holds the opposition; in a king-and-pawn ending it often decides who wins.
The basic rule is a default for pure king-and-pawn endings; confirm any position with the tablebase.
contrasts: A king-and-pawn position can look like a win and be a draw when one king step gives the defender the opposition.
Which side of the board the ending is on does not matter: a mirror image gives the same result.
